title: Food4Gut multicenter randomized placebo-controlled trial
author: Sophie Hiel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.baidica6
materials: Prof. M. Cnop, M.D., Ph.D. (Hôpital Erasme)

Exclusion criteria for the study are listed below:
Pregnancy in progress or planned within 6 months;
Saliva samples (for the measure of amylase activity).
Evaluation of hepatic fibrosis and/or steatosis:

steps.title: Recruit eligible participants
steps.instruction: Identify obese patients (BMI ≥ 25 kg·m⁻²) with at least one listed comorbidity (pre‑diabetes, diabetes, dyslipidemia, NAFLD) across the three hospitals, exclude those with psychiatric issues, antipsychotic use, recent antibiotics/probiotics/prebiotics (<6 weeks), special diets, or unacceptable food‑product test, and aim for 50 participants per centre (total ≈ 150).

steps.title: Obtain informed consent
steps.instruction: During the screening visit, explain the experimental procedure, provide study documents, and have the patient sign the informed consent form.

steps.title: Randomize and blind participants
steps.instruction: Assign each consented participant, in a single‑blinded manner, to either the treatment arm (inulin) or the placebo arm (maltodextrin).

steps.title: Distribute supplement and diet materials
steps.instruction: Give the treatment group daily inulin (Fibruline®) and the placebo group daily maltodextrin (C*Dry A 01318, Cargill) together with a recipe book and diet‑ician‑provided dietary advice to increase consumption of fructan‑rich vegetables.

substeps.instruction: Week 1: 8 g of supplement in the morning.
Weeks 2‑end: 8 g in the morning + 8 g at lunch and dinner (total 16 g day⁻¹).

steps.title: Prohibit other microbiota‑modifying agents
steps.instruction: Instruct participants to avoid any probiotics or prebiotics not supplied by the study, as well as antibiotics, during the entire intervention period.

steps.title: Schedule dietician follow‑ups
steps.instruction: Arrange dietician meetings at baseline (M0), month 1 (M1), month 2 (M2), month 3 (M3) and also at the end of the first and second month; during each meeting collect a one‑week dietary recall questionnaire.

steps.title: Monitor side‑effects
steps.instruction: Provide participants with a daily questionnaire to record gastrointestinal or other adverse events during the first week of supplementation and at each subsequent dietician visit.

steps.title: Conduct baseline and 3‑month test days
steps.instruction: At M0 and M3 perform the full set of clinical, biochemical, and behavioral assessments as listed below.

substeps.instruction: Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT): draw fasting blood at –20 min, –10 min, –5 min; give 75 g glucose (time 0); draw blood at 10, 30, 60, 90, 120 min for glucose, insulin and C‑peptide.
Collect fasting blood for:
‑ Lipid profile (HDL‑C, triglycerides, total cholesterol, free fatty acids).
‑ Inflammatory biomarkers (IL‑1β, IL‑17a, IL‑8, MCP‑1, TNF‑α).
‑ Liver enzymes and related markers (ALT, AST, α‑2‑macroglobulin, haptoglobin, Apo‑A1, GGT, total bilirubin) for FibroTest® calculation.
Collect stool sample (home or hospital) for:
‑ 16S rDNA gene sequencing and qPCR of specific bacteria.
‑ Transfer to germ‑free mice (MNUT lab) and in‑vitro fermentation studies.
Collect morning urine for metabolomics analysis.
Measure anthropometrics: height, weight, hip circumference, waist circumference; calculate BMI and waist‑to‑hip ratio.
Measure blood pressure.
Perform bio‑impedancemetry for body‑fat and lean‑mass assessment.
Perform FibroScan® to obtain liver stiffness (elasticity) and Controlled Attenuation Parameter (CAP).
If indicated, perform abdominal CT‑scan to quantify visceral and subcutaneous fat areas and muscle mass.
Administer behavioral questionnaires:
‑ Questionnaire for Eating Disorder Diagnoses (Q‑EDD).
‑ French version of the Dutch Eating Behavior Questionnaire (DEBQ).
‑ Additional tests for cognitive flexibility, fear‑message sensitivity, and individual vulnerability (IPSY/PSYULB teams).
Administer International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) for physical‑activity reporting.

steps.title: Handle severe liver findings
steps.instruction: If FibroScan® indicates a high risk of cirrhosis, arrange a standard‑care liver biopsy; during bariatric surgery, obtain liver biopsy and, if possible, visceral and subcutaneous adipose‑tissue biopsies for inflammation analysis.

steps.title: Record and store all data
steps.instruction: Enter all clinical, biochemical, imaging, questionnaire, and adverse‑event data into the study database for later statistical analysis.
